gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 identifies the same unsupported root-N empirical covariance bound under finite-second-moment/P2 assumptions, supplies the same heavy-tail obstruction, and specifies the needed additional moment and dependence conditions.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both identify the failure of transferring a universal O(N^{-1/2}) covariance-estimation rate from finite second moments to the full P2 setting; both recognize that heavier moment and dependence assumptions are required.

component_coverage.gold_component: The claimed root-N empirical covariance rate is unsupported under only finite second moments/P2 assumptions, including admissible heavy-tailed laws.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states that finite second moments do not justify the root-N covariance bound, gives a finite-variance heavy-tailed counterexample with slower error, and explains that the mean-field justification does not cover all P2 inputs.

component_coverage.gold_component: The adequate repair is to condition the rate on finite fourth moments and appropriate dependence assumptions while leaving population-level results unchanged.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly requires additional moment and dependence hypotheses and distinguishes the auxiliary finite-sample rate from the P2 assumptions governing exactness results.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-011 identifies the same missing 1/(N-1) normalization in the centered anomaly-based ETKF covariance transform, derives the resulting incorrect covariance and possible non-positive-semidefiniteness, and gives the corresponding correction.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both identify the ETKF normalization defect: using the unnormalized centered anomaly matrix in the transform omits the 1/(N-1) factor, so the constructed covariance has an oversized decrement and the square-root formula may fail.

component_coverage.gold_component: The ETKF anomaly transform uses an incorrectly normalized second-moment formula, producing an extra factor N-1 in the covariance decrement.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly says the anomaly matrix is unnormalized and derives the resulting covariance as Cf-(N-1)Cf H^T S^{-1}H Cf instead of the stated analysis covariance.

component_coverage.gold_component: The oversized decrement can make the square-root argument indefinite and violates the advertised covariance condition.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction supplies a concrete non-positive-semidefinite example and states that the ETKF square root may fail to exist and generally does not meet the analysis-covariance condition.

component_coverage.gold_component: The repair is to insert 1/(N-1) consistently in the ETKF transform and related Gram-matrix formula, without changing the separate joint-sample projection formula.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction identifies the same missing factor in the related Gram matrix and prescribes consistent normalization while distinguishing the later projection formula that does not need it.
